en.title: Fill in Positive Integers to Make Two Rows of Blocks Sum Equally
en.description:
Replace every 0 in the two arrays with an arbitrary positive integer, keeping the other values unchanged, so that the two totals are equal and as small as possible; output −1 if there is no solution. The filled values are not limited by the original arrays' upper bound of 10000.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site; missing numeric bounds and recoveries of source typos are all stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line contains rowA, and the third line contains rowB; 1≤n,m≤100000, original elements 0..10000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3; -1; 2. These answers were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Filling each row's 0s with 1 gives its minimum sum; a row containing a 0 can increase to any larger integer, while a row without 0s has a fixed total. Take the larger of the two minimum sums, then check whether a fixed row equals it.
